researcher_notes: This category confirms the task's working hypothesis: payments vendors overwhelmingly do not name restaurant-brand customers in ordinary marketing copy, because acquiring/processing relationships are frequently confidential or white-labeled through a POS partner. Six of thirteen vendors (Stripe, TSYS, Elavon, Priority Technology Holdings, Paysafe, North/Payment Depot) came back thin or empty despite targeted searching, consistent with instructions to not manufacture matches. The strongest evidence source in this whole batch was NOT press releases but Global Payments' Q1 FY2026 earnings call (May 6, 2026 transcript, fetched directly), which named five restaurant brands in one call (CKE Restaurants/Hardee's/Carl's Jr., Subway, KFC, Pizza Hut, Bojangles) as recent Genius platform wins -- a reminder that earnings-call transcripts are a high-yield, underused primary source for this kind of research. Two important cautions on those five records: (1) several are explicitly about Genius sub-modules (kitchen management for Subway, digital menu for Bojangles, unspecified module for KFC/Pizza Hut in APAC) rather than confirmed core payments/acquiring, so per the task's conflation warning I scored vendor_role 'unknown' rather than 'acquirer_or_payments' wherever the quoted language did not explicitly say Global Payments is the payments/acquiring provider (CKE Restaurants is the one exception with explicit 'in-store payments provider' language, scored acquirer_or_payments with High confidence); (2) none included explicit 'all locations' or 'brand-wide' language, so none were scored as brand-wide/enterprise-wide even where a large unit count was given. This category also surfaced a major corporate-structure event that changes how several graph entities should be understood going forward: on January 9, 2026, Global Payments completed a $24.3B acquisition of Worldpay from FIS and GTCR, and simultaneously divested its own Issuer Solutions business (the operation still commonly called 'TSYS' after Global Payments' 2019 TSYS merger) to FIS for $13.5B, where it is now marketed as 'FIS Total Issuing Solutions.' Concretely this means: Worldpay is no longer FIS/GTCR-owned -- it is now a Global Payments-owned brand, which may eventually mean today's 'Worldpay' and 'Global Payments' vendor entities in the graph converge; and 'TSYS' as an independent or Global-Payments-owned brand should be treated as folded/retired, now living inside FIS rather than Global Payments -- I did not find (and would not expect to find) named restaurant-merchant customer evidence for TSYS/Issuer Solutions specifically, since issuer processing serves card-issuing banks, not merchants, so restaurant-brand customer evidence is the wrong evidence type for this entity regardless of ownership. Separately, CardFree (one of the 13 vendors on the approved list) was itself acquired by Fiserv on September 5, 2025 to bolster Clover's hospitality/restaurant capabilities -- it is no longer an independent company, though I kept it as its own line per the approved vendor list and attributed its named customers (Dunkin', Lazy Dog Restaurants, both from the Fiserv acquisition-announcement coverage rather than a dedicated CardFree case study) to it directly. North also is a 2024 rebrand of North American Bancard; I could not independently confirm in this pass whether 'Payment Depot' is the same corporate entity/sibling brand or a separate company, so I am flagging that as unresolved rather than asserting it. I checked the 2026-07-21 research archive's 936-row candidate_evidence and 38-row verified_seed_evidence arrays for any rows tagged to these 13 vendors (matching on Vendor Archive/Vendor fields and a full-text scan for vendor names) and found zero overlap -- that archive only crawled coates, crunchtime, olo, par, paytronix, qu, r365, thanx, presto, and toast, none of which are Payments-category vendors, so nothing could be reused for this batch and all 15 records below come from fresh research.

records.brand: CKE Restaurants Holdings (Hardee's and Carl's Jr.)
records.confidence_rationale: Direct quote from Global Payments' own Q1 FY2026 earnings call transcript (fetched primary source, not secondary summary): 'CKE Restaurants Holdings, Inc. selected Genius as its exclusive U.S. point-of-sale software and will also use Global Payments as its in-store payments provider for its iconic Hardee's and Carl's Jr. brands, deploying our solutions across more than 2,400 corporate and franchise locations.' Corroborated by Investing.com trade coverage with the same figure.
records.notes: Also corroborated by https://ca.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/global-payments-wins-cke-restaurants-pos-deal-for-2400-sites-93CH-4625985 (2026-05-11), which quotes the deal as covering 'more than 2,400 corporate and franchise restaurant locations across the U.S.' This is the one Global Payments record in this batch with explicit payments-provider language (not just a POS/adjacent-module purchase), so it is the strongest, least ambiguous record found for this vendor. Not scored brand_wide_deployment because neither source uses 'all locations' or 'brand-wide' language, even though 2,400+ is a large majority of CKE's combined Hardee's/Carl's Jr. footprint.

records.confidence_rationale: Direct quote from the same Q1 FY2026 earnings call transcript: 'Subway recently selected our Genius kitchen management software deployment across approximately 2,500 locations.' Primary-source quote with a specific unit count, but the named product is explicitly kitchen management, not payments/acquiring -- following the task's instruction not to conflate adjacent Genius modules with a confirmed payments relationship, vendor_role is set to 'unknown' rather than 'acquirer_or_payments.'
records.notes: Distinct from Subway's separate, much older Adyen relationship recorded below (payments platform, announced 2020) -- large multi-brand chains like Subway can and do run different vendors for different technology layers simultaneously, this is not a data conflict, just two separate real relationships in two separate product categories/vendors.

records.confidence_rationale: Direct quote from the Q1 FY2026 earnings call transcript: 'In Asia Pacific, we were pleased to be selected by KFC and Pizza Hut.' Primary-source quote naming the brand, but no product module, unit count, or country-level detail given, so vendor_role is left 'unknown' rather than assuming a payments/acquiring relationship specifically.
records.notes: KFC's Asia Pacific markets are operated by a mix of Yum China (separate public company) and regional master franchisees; this quote does not specify which KFC APAC markets/operators are covered.

records.confidence_rationale: Same earnings-call sentence as the KFC record above names Pizza Hut alongside KFC with identical lack of product/scope detail.
records.notes: Recorded as a separate line from KFC since they are legally and operationally distinct brands under Yum!, even though this single sentence names both together with no differentiation.

records.confidence_rationale: Earnings-call quote: 'Bojangles purchased our digital menu solutions for its corporate-owned stores, expanding our long-standing relationship' -- the phrase 'long-standing relationship' implies a pre-existing (unspecified) Global Payments relationship with Bojangles, but the only concretely named new item is digital menu boards, not payments processing. Corroborated by a separate, independent source (QSR Magazine/Hi Auto, 2025-12-04) describing Bojangles' voice-AI drive-thru system running on a 'Genius XPI integration' live across 'almost 500 restaurants' as of December 2025 -- this is the source of the unit-count-based deployment_status classification, not the earnings call itself.
records.notes: Secondary corroborating source: https://www.qsrmagazine.com/news/hi-auto-and-bojangles-reveal-game-changing-voice-ai-features-at-global-payments-genius-conference/ (2025-12-04), which describes Bojangles' Hi Auto voice-AI ordering system integrating with Global Payments' 'Genius XPI' across a deployment that scaled from 100 to 300 to nearly 500 locations. Neither source explicitly confirms Global Payments is Bojangles' core in-store payments acquirer at those ~500 locations -- treat the payments-specific portion of this relationship as unconfirmed, only the POS-platform-adjacent integration (digital menu + Genius XPI) is directly evidenced.

records.confidence_rationale: Vendor press release (PR Newswire) naming Subway directly and describing Adyen as its selected payments partner for North America locations, with a 'one integration' and franchisee-dashboard/reconciliation framing appropriate for a large franchise system.
records.notes: No specific unit count given beyond describing Subway as 'the world's largest quick service restaurant by restaurant count.' This is an older (2020), separate, and product-distinct relationship from Subway's 2026 Global Payments Genius kitchen-management deal recorded above -- both can be true simultaneously for different technology layers.

records.brand: Five Guys and Blaze Pizza (Cypress Five Star franchisee, Canada)
records.confidence_rationale: Vendor press release with an explicit, specific location count and named franchisee operator: 'Adyen and Cypress Five Star, Inc., a leading franchise operator, are teaming up to bring unified payments across their 60 Five Guys locations in Canada.' Cypress Five Star is confirmed as the exclusive Five Guys/Blaze Pizza franchisee for specific Canadian provinces, not the brands' owning companies.
records.notes: Explicitly one Canadian franchisee's 60 Five Guys locations (of 75 total sites Cypress Five Star operates across both brands) -- not a Five Guys-wide or Blaze Pizza-wide corporate decision. Do not conflate with brand-standard adoption.

records.confidence_rationale: Vendor/trade press release (PR Newswire APAC, corroborated by Payments Dive and Fast Casual) naming Guzman y Gomez as an Adyen payments customer, but explicitly scoped to its Singapore locations, not the brand's home Australian market or global footprint.
records.notes: Guzman y Gomez is headquartered in Australia; this deal is specific to its (much smaller) Singapore market entry, so vendor_role is set to regional_deployment rather than implying a brand-wide relationship.

records.confidence_rationale: Vendor press release naming the operator group and its CFO as a named quote source for the SkyTab Business Intelligence launch, describing Live! as a SkyTab BI customer.
records.notes: Live! Hospitality & Entertainment operates dining, entertainment, gaming, hotel, and sports-anchored venues (55M+ annual visitors) -- it is a hospitality/entertainment operator with substantial food & beverage operations rather than a pure standalone restaurant chain, similar in kind to the Agilysys hotel-embedded-F&B scope question flagged in the POS batch. No unit count for the F&B-specific locations running SkyTab was given. Beyond this record, extensive searching for a named, dated, major QSR/casual-dining SkyTab enterprise customer (as opposed to product launch announcements) did not surface one -- this despite Shift4's own SkyTab being a real, actively marketed restaurant payments+POS product, so this category may simply be underdisclosed by Shift4 rather than absent.

records.confidence_rationale: Vendor press release with an explicit unit count: Taco John's deploying the FreedomPay Commerce Platform 'across more than 400 locations.'
records.notes: This is an older record (2013); current status as of 2026 not reconfirmed in this pass. Taco John's total system size at the time was in a similar range to the 400+ cited, so this was likely a near-full-chain deployment even though the release does not use explicit 'all locations' language.

records.confidence_rationale: Vendor/operator press release (GlobeNewswire, corroborated by PaymentsJournal, QSR Magazine, Fast Casual, Hospitality Technology) with an explicit unit count: Shake Shack implementing FreedomPay's Next Level Commerce / Touchless Commerce solutions 'across over 200 locations in the United States,' standardizing payments across in-store, online, and in-app channels.
records.notes: Shake Shack's U.S. footprint was larger than 200 locations by 2021, so this is a significant but not stated-as-complete rollout; no 'all locations' language used.

records.confidence_rationale: Named in trade press coverage of Fiserv's acquisition of CardFree: 'CardFree's software is used by restaurants, hotels and breweries, including Dunkin' and Lazy Dog Restaurants' (Payments Dive, corroborated by Fiserv's own investor-relations press release using near-identical language). This is a named-customer claim carried in acquisition coverage rather than a dedicated CardFree case study, and gives no unit count, region, or deployment date for the Dunkin' relationship itself.
records.notes: CardFree was founded by the team that built the original Starbucks and Dunkin' mobile apps, which is likely why Dunkin' is named -- this may reflect a longstanding relationship rather than one dated to 2025; exact start date not found. IMPORTANT: CardFree was acquired by Fiserv on 2025-09-05 and is being integrated into Clover and Commerce Hub -- it is no longer an independent company (see vendors_flagged_as_possibly_defunct_or_renamed).

records.confidence_rationale: Same source and same caveats as the Dunkin' record above -- named alongside Dunkin' in Fiserv's CardFree acquisition coverage as an existing CardFree software customer, with no unit count, date, or scope detail for this specific relationship.
records.notes: Lazy Dog Restaurants is a ~50-unit U.S. casual-dining chain. Same corporate-status caveat as above: CardFree is now a Fiserv subsidiary, not independent.

records.confidence_rationale: Vendor press release (corroborated by Hospitality Technology, Fast Company) explicitly describing this as a pilot: Fiserv's 'Checkless Payments' concept, co-designed with USHG Executive Chairman Danny Meyer, 'is currently being piloted in Manhatta, USHG's award-winning fine dining restaurant, before being rolled out to restaurants leveraging the Clover Hospitality system.'
records.notes: Single-restaurant pilot within one USHG property, explicitly framed as a precursor to a broader Clover Hospitality rollout rather than a current deployed relationship at scale. This is the clearest dated, named-restaurant evidence found for Fiserv's own (non-CardFree, non-Clover-generic) payments/commerce technology; broader Clover merchant-acquiring relationships with major restaurant chains were searched for but not found with comparable specificity -- Clover's restaurant-facing marketing relies on aggregate scale claims ('nearly 200,000 restaurants worldwide') rather than named chains, consistent with the POS batch's finding for Clover.

records.confidence_rationale: Vendor case study naming the operator group and several of its restaurant brands (Carluccio's, Cinnamon Collection, Giraffe Restaurants, Ed's Easy Diner, Fishworks, Gourmet Burger Kitchen, Slim Chickens) with more than 100 U.K. sites, and naming the specific product (Worldpay Total Hospitality) implemented for the Carluccio's brand specifically.
records.notes: No publication date shown on the case study page; '2026' reflects capture date, not confirmed original publish date. Boparan Restaurant Group is a U.K. multi-brand operator, not a single restaurant brand -- Worldpay Total Hospitality is named specifically in connection with the Carluccio's brand within this group, not confirmed across all of Boparan's brands. IMPORTANT CORPORATE-STATUS NOTE: Worldpay was acquired by Global Payments (GPN) from FIS and GTCR in a transaction that closed January 9, 2026 (~$24.3B) -- as of this research date Worldpay is no longer FIS/GTCR-owned; it is now a Global Payments-owned entity (see researcher_notes and vendors_flagged_as_possibly_defunct_or_renamed). Given this, current/future Worldpay customer relationships may increasingly be reported under the Global Payments corporate umbrella rather than as standalone Worldpay press releases.

vendors_with_thin_or_no_evidence: Stripe -- private company; extensive searching found only third-party ordering/restaurant-tech platforms (e.g. Dines, Spades) that use Stripe as underlying payment infrastructure, not restaurant brands themselves named as direct Stripe customers. No dated, named restaurant-chain case study located.

TSYS -- see vendors_flagged_as_possibly_defunct_or_renamed; the business now sits inside FIS as 'Total Issuing Solutions' and serves card-issuing banks, not merchants, so restaurant-brand customer evidence is not the applicable evidence type for this entity even in principle.

Elavon -- U.S. Bank subsidiary; only very small independent restaurant examples found (Rami's Cafe and Pete's Restaurant in Knoxville, TN; a case study referencing 'Yee-Haw'), none are recognizable chains, and none carried usable publication dates.

Priority Technology Holdings (PRTH) -- public company with a named restaurant-facing product (MX POS), but no dated press release or case study naming a specific restaurant chain customer was found despite searching investor materials and trade press.

Paysafe (PSFE) -- public company; only a small independent franchise (Crazy Pita Rotisserie & Grill) was found in a customer-spotlight page, undated, and general partnership marketing with order-ahead vendor Applova with no named restaurant chain attached.

North / Payment Depot -- North is a 2024 rebrand of North American Bancard with restaurant POS/payments marketing pages, but no dated named restaurant-chain customer was found. Additionally, the relationship between 'North' and 'Payment Depot' (same company, sibling brand, or separate company) could not be independently confirmed in this research pass -- flagging as unresolved rather than asserting a specific corporate relationship.
vendors_flagged_as_possibly_defunct_or_r: Worldpay -- no longer FIS/GTCR-owned. Global Payments (GPN) completed its acquisition of Worldpay from FIS and GTCR on January 9, 2026 for approximately $24.3B (concurrently divesting Global Payments' own Issuer Solutions/former-TSYS business to FIS for $13.5B). As of this research date, Worldpay is a Global Payments-owned brand. This is a significant, recent (2026) corporate event that should inform how the graph models the Worldpay entity going forward -- it may increasingly converge with or be reported alongside the Global Payments entity rather than remaining a wholly separate corporate line.

TSYS -- effectively folded/retired as an independent or Global-Payments-owned brand. Global Payments acquired TSYS in 2019 and had operated its Issuer Solutions business under that lineage since; as part of the January 2026 three-way Global Payments/Worldpay/FIS transaction, Global Payments divested that Issuer Solutions business to FIS, where it is now marketed as 'FIS Total Issuing Solutions.' No current independent 'TSYS' branded entity should be expected; treat historical TSYS-branded restaurant relationships (if any are later found) as most likely superseded and now attributable to Global Payments (2019-2026) or FIS (2026-present) depending on the date.

CardFree -- acquired by Fiserv on September 5, 2025 to expand Clover's hospitality/restaurant capabilities (drive-through software, kiosk/sub-inventory enablement, loyalty/delivery/property-management integrations). No longer an independently operated company, though kept as its own vendor line per the approved list since the CardFree product/brand name persists through the integration.

North -- rebranded from North American Bancard in 2024. Not defunct, but the entity name has changed; historical 'North American Bancard' references and current 'North' references describe the same company.
